title: Congressional caseworkers report easier reporting and case handling with Civic Revere
summary: Staff in Representative Moulton’s office report easier workflows with Civic Revere, but the interview does not separate AI from conventional software improvements.
account: Representative Seth Moulton’s office had worked with Civic as a design partner since about early 2025. House spending records show that from April to June 2026 the office paid Indigovern LLC and Housecall LLC each month for technology services and that no House office paid a vendor named Civic in that quarter. In an August 2026 interview that Civic staff wrote and published, caseworkers Danielle Leahy and Claudia Runk from the office described their role in developing Revere. They reported that the platform displayed casework patterns automatically and made it easier to reopen cases while keeping their history. They described reduced mental effort and time demands, without a measured time comparison. The interview concerns the full workflow, including conventional software features, and does not isolate the contribution of AI. Civic’s inventory submission states that it had no quantitative evidence yet and that its system uses OpenAI’s GPT-4o. Civic’s current product page identifies AI-supported tagging, clustering, urgent-case flagging, and retrieval over office records.
